label: sec:nuclear-binding-intro
html: Once the two-nucleon isospin channel is selected, extending the linear-programming deficit profile across the (Z, N) lattice determines the global stability landscape of composite nuclei. This section defines the LP demand profile and demand stability criterion, proves that the nuclear binding operator partitions the (Z, N) chart into three distinct structural regimes—the torus-knot regime for light nuclei, the Hopf-link regime across intermediate shells, and the post-magic regime above closed shells—and formulates the periodic-table demand conjecture linking deficit minima to the empirical magic numbers.
